newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan forex stance accepted by G7 countries - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan forex stance accepted by G7 countries - MOF.

text.p: Japan's view that an excessively weak or strong yen is unfavourable was accepted by the Group of Seven (G7) countries during their meeting over the weekend, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee meeting on Monday.
He said this was reflected in the statement issued by the G7 after the meeting. He added that the countries also agreed on Japan's view that cooperation among G7 nations should be maintained.
"Our view that excessive weakness in the yen as well as excessive strength in the yen is unfavourable and that G7 cooperation should be maintained was accepted (by other G7 nations)," Mitsuzuka said.
He said that the G7 nations agreed in their statement that the major misalignments in exchange markets noted in the group's April 1995 communique had been corrected.

They also reaffirmed their views that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility is undesirable. They also agreed to monitor developments on currency markets and to cooperate as appropriate, he said.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told the same committee meeting that Japan was able to secure comments it wanted from G7 nations.
Hashimoto added that cooperative ties among G7 nations remain steadfast.
